children: The White House expressed disappointment on Wednesday following the Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates, calling the move “rather unfortunate” and arguing it lacked a "compelling economic case."
In a decisive move to rein in stubbornly high inflation, the central bank
its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point and signaled further tightening ahead as the U.S. economy continues to run hotter than expected.

In an interview with Fox News, White House spokesman Kush Desai emphasized that President Donald Trump had been “abundantly clear” about his opposition to further rate increases. Desai contested the necessity of the hike, noting that inflation has cooled by almost every metric since the Federal Open Market Committee last convened.

“I think the president has been abundantly clear on where he wanted interest rates to go," Desai said. "And certainly, today’s rather unfortunate decision by the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates was not, from the administration’s point of view, backed by a particularly compelling economic case."

Desai told Fox News that inflation now is entirely the result of an energy supply shock driven by the ongoing war in the Middle East, asserting that this geopolitical factor "has nothing to do with interest rates."
Looking ahead, the White House warned that the central bank's tightening monetary policy could stall the nation's economic momentum.

"All higher interest rates are gonna do right now is stop any significant progress that the United States has made under the president," Desai said, pointing specifically to the negative impact that rising mortgage rates will have on American consumers.

title: White House criticizes Federal Reserve's 'unfortunate' rate hike
